utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can't answer. This makes it difficult, because I put questions to you and you can't answer these. I don't know whether you understand what I'm asking you or whether, at your level, you were not able to, so let me address the question from a different angle. This document you have before you, which is signed by the HVO and the ABiH, which you were aware of, according to you does this document show that at the time, at least, in Konjic that between the HVO and the ABiH, there is no major conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document clearly states that not only there were no major, there were no conflicts whatsoever in Konjic at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are saying that there was no conflict at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you said that there were approximately 85 kilometres between Prozor and Konjic, and the document we have before us indicates that an agreement was signed between the commander of the ABiH in Konjic and the commander of the HVO to make sure that those events that occurred in Prozor could not happen again in Konjic. So this is my question: Where you were in Konjic, had you understood what had happened precisely in Prozor? Who was behind this situation, according to you, if you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not in a command position. I told you that I was assistant commander for operations and training. So I was informed only to the extent that I needed to know at that point in time. Perhaps my commander knew more, but I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, we spoke about movements, and I pointed out the previous document and why it was important to prevent any movement of units. Now, would you please look at 2D799. This is a letter signed -- this is in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this is signed by the Main Staff of the Supreme Command of Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 25th of October, and it says that the purpose of this letter is to establish the extent of responsibility of Zahir Hrnjica. And then it says on the 25th of October, 1992, Mr. Zahir Hrnjica failed to carry out an order of the Main Staff of the Supreme Command of Armed Forces, to carry out a safe escort of a company of the Municipal Defence Staff of Gornji Vakuf between Konjic and Parsovic. Mr. Zahir Hrnjica, as a commander of the 1st Klisani Battalion, came to the Konjic municipality to warn that he would not allow any movement of units of the BH Army in the territory of Neretvica and that, if necessary, he would prevent it by way of weapons. Based on this document, Mr. Juric, it is clear that Mr. Divjak, on behalf of the Main Staff of the Supreme Command of Armed Forces wants this case investigated and established how this came about. Let me ask you first, did you know Mr. Zahir Hrnjica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: I knew him as commander, but we did not have much contact.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know why Mr. Zahir Hrnjica did not allow any units to pass through the territory of Konjic municipality on their way to Prozor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Well, this conduct of his is precisely based on the report written earlier about not allowing any units to pass via our territory, the territory controlled by us, the HVO, and the BH Army units.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we hear once again why you had this view that no units should be allowed to pass via your territory on their way to Prozor? Why did you have this firm position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Well, that was clear, because had we allowed any units to pass through, then conflict would have most likely spread to Konjic as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, would you please look at 2D806. This is a report by a group or, rather, by a commission of the 4th Corps, dated the 17th of December, 1992. We can see here that in the previous document, the request to allow passage through Konjic municipality was signed by Mr. Divjak. Now, would you look at the second page of this document, page 2, paragraph 3. It says: "Commission of the 4th Corps on the 7th of December, 1992, states, when speaking of Colonel Divjak, that they suspected him of being involved with Zejnil in various activities in Prozor municipality and creating conflict between Croats and Muslims so that there should be a war in a wider area, so that Muslims would be drawn into a war with Croats." Now, Zejnil mentioned here, and you can see this on the basis of the document, is Zejnil Delalic. Is this a person who lived in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Occasionally, at the time, he did live in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Based on this position of the 4th Corps, can it be concluded that they were accusing Mr. Divjak and Zejnil of creating conflict in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, had the units passed through, based on the previous order of the BH Army, had they passed via Konjic, would that have caused conflict in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Konjic and in the wider surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Could we look at 2D255, please. This is a document signed by Mr. Arif Pasalic on the 16th of January, 1993, and he states, once again, on the basis of an order of the Supreme Command, to ensure military control of all incoming/outgoing traffic and to set up a check-point. Now, was this check-point established and why -- if so, why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: The check-point in Bradina was controlled by the MUP of Konjic municipality previously, and in the MUP of Konjic there was a mixed composition, Croats and Muslims, working together. Now, with the establishment of this check-point at Bradina, what is sought for here is control and insight into what our fighters were doing, the ones that had been at the training centre, and this was in cooperation with the TO. And they had nothing against this and said it was a good thing that people should be trained in the area of weapons, explosives, and the like. And looking at this and seeing who it was addressed to and sent to, I can say that what I said earlier on, that is to say, that it was the leaders of the BH Army who were seeking to affect a conflict in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now look at 2D771 now, please, and we'll comment on it just briefly, because this is taking up too much time. Tell me when you've found the document, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This document was signed by Mr. Sagolj --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this document dates back to January, but I'd like to go back in time because I'm more interested in October 23rd, 1992, and what happened in Prozor. I'm trying to understand the questions put to you by Ms. Nozica, but so far it's not really clear in my mind and I need to ask some questions to see if I really understand what she's trying to demonstrate. According to the few documents we have seen, who are in-house documents of the BiH and the 4th Corps, it seems that -- I might be wrong, but it seems that the events in Prozor could be blamed on some Muslim elements which would have committed a number of things that led to the conflict, whereas in other regions, like in your region, there was no conflict. Now, according to you, is this a credible assumption; i.e., could we think that what occurred in Prozor could not be blamed on the HVO, but should be blamed on elements of the ABiH who disregarded the orders and committed some actions which led to what happened in Prozor? Can you confirm this assumption or do you believe that it is not a correct assumption?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, from these documents, the ones we've just gone through, and in the way you explained them, my conclusion is certain elements of the BH Army were included in this conflict in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is also your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when you say that you don't know where these questions are leading, it puts me in a rather difficult position, but we'll take it step by step and we'll see how the conflict in Konjic came about. And that's why we're taking it this way, but we'll get to the crux of the matter very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, have you found the document? Just tell me who signed it. Who was Mr. Sagolj? We can see that at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Herceg Stjepan HVO Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, this report, sent to the HVO Mostar, to the Command of the Operative Zone, the Operations Department, the IPD, Information and Propaganda Department, once again speaks about a joint meeting, and that's important, attended by all the commanders of the HVO and BiH, the BH Staff in Konjic, the president of the War Presidency, the HVO president, and the president of the MUP, with the aim of sizing up the security situation and taking specific activities to diffuse the growing tensions between the two ethnic groups. The following conclusion was reached at the meeting: A, conflicts between the Croats and Muslims, as a method, should be ruled out, and an order should be issued to the level of platoons; then, B, urgently call a meeting of representatives of the 4th Corps in the Operative Zone of the HVO and to implement the decisions already reached with respect to housing in a single building. Now, Mr. Juric, were you ever informed by your commanders that a meeting of this kind took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, at that time, and we're talking about the 21st of January here, were attempts still being made by your brigade, the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, and the representative of the BH Army to prevent a conflict from breaking out in Konjic; is that what follows from this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, this joint meeting shows precisely that, and these important conclusions were made whereby a conflicts should be prevented at all costs between the HVO and the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, I'm emphasizing the date of this meeting, which is the 21st of January. Now look at 2D814, and this is an order from Mr. Sefer Halilovic, the Supreme Command Staff of the armed forces, and the date is the 28th of January. He says here: "We have information that in the areas of Jablanica, Konjic, Pazaric and Turcin, and we'll deal with Konjic that a small part of the BH Army, police and other authorities are probably in other areas too have fully sided with the Greater Croatia policy and are implementing orders received from the Establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and this is having a direct impact upon our struggle for the unified and democratic BH ..."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel kindly slow down when reading the document, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We have from Tufo from Hadzic and Cerovac, Midhad, the commander of the Konjic Brigade, and he is issuing an order here to investigate, to see what the situation is like, to talk to Arif Pasalic -- Fikret Alipasic [phoen]. Now, Mr. Juric, may we have your comments on this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: If I link this document up to the previous one that we've already looked at, then we can clearly see in this document that specific people are referred to who were in Konjic, occupying these various posts, and the people attending the meeting, where it was stated loud and clear that a conflict in Konjic must not be allowed to break out. And now this is being sent -- the order, or the commander, or whatever, is sent so that these people can be checked out. So I stand by what I've already said, and that is that the conflict between us Croats and the Muslims in Konjic was staged precisely in the Supreme Command in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now look at page 2 of this document, please, which is the ERN number you have here, and it says that it is sent to the commander, Safet Bozic in Jablanica, and it says: "Safet, you should go to Konjic and issue a serious caution to Guska, Jasmin, because of his cooperation with the HVO and disclosing the positions of the BH Army." Now, could you tell us who the doctor was that is signed here at the bottom? Who was referred to as the doctor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: That was Cibo, Safet, and I've already said at the end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993, he became the president of the War Presidency. He was appointed by President Alija Izetbegovic as president of the War Presidency Konjic and Jablanica municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And who did he replace?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: He replaced the man who we had good contact with and cooperation, and that was Rusmir -- Dr. Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's equip over the next document, which once again indicates attempts to maintain good cooperation, and let's move on to P1675, the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm trying to understand, because this is very complicated and you might be able to help us. This document from Halilovic seems to be questioning a number of people in Konjic, a number of people who are actually mentioned, but he also says that some people seem to be implied --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Involved, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Involved in this notion of Greater Croatia. Now, this is my question: At your level, did you ever hear about Greater Croatia, did you ever hear about what some people were doing, or are you discovering this for the first time today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm learning about this just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, the Croats from Konjic had never heard about these notions of Greater Croatia and didn't discuss this among each other, or did you discuss these notions among each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this kind of thing couldn't have been discussed in Konjic, because the ratio between Muslims and Croats, in terms of numbers of inhabitants, there were far fewer Croats, perhaps just a third or even less than a third, so the Croats couldn't have accomplished what you've just said, this greater Croatian state or whatever you just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, I'm just going to ask you something. I'm going to ask a follow-up question to what Judge Antonetti just asked you. For example, in April 1994, did you fight for Bosnia-Herzegovina? I meant to say "April 1993." Did you fight for Bosnia-Herzegovina, together with the BH Army, and did you make public statements to that effect?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did fight for Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I did make public statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber where and when you made these public statements or announcements?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: When I came to be the brigade commander, some 20 days after that I granted an interview to a paper in Konjic, and the editorial board of that paper, and I described to them my life and ended up by making a conclusion and stating what the object of my struggle was. So that's it, and that was as deputy commander, actually, of the brigade when I made that statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Now, I would like to tell the Trial Chamber that I do have that newspaper article. Mr. Juric brought it with him when he arrived here, not before. I've had it translated, so he we can place it on the ELMO, if necessary, and then we can have it interpreted to see what his positions were in April 1993. Now, I said we'd skip a document, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we're now discovering that you have granted an interview. We didn't know this, but you just told us. And you said that you were fighting for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but this feeling that you had and that you expressed in this newspaper article, was it shared by all your Croat friends within the brigade or was it your own feeling? Were you the only one to feel this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can just speak in my own name, but I can also give you my opinions, and I shared the view of most of the Croat inhabitants of Konjic when I said what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Juric, take a look at document P1675. You can skip over one and find 1675. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: 1675, you say?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's a letter signed by Mr. Sefer Halilovic, and he's writing it on the 17th of March, 1993. And let me ask you first, Mr. Juric: When did the conflict -- or, rather, was there an attack launched by the BH Army against the HVO in March, and what was the date, if it did?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 23rd of March, 1993, was when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, fine. So we can look at the document now. Mr. Sefer Halilovic is writing to the Main Staff of the HVO, and he says that in Sarajevo, Mr. Arif Pasalic spent some time in Sarajevo and that he informed him of developments in the area of Herzegovina and beyond. And he says at the end: "I propose that Pasalic visit you and inform you of our views of existing problems and how we see the possibility of overcoming them. I hope that this aspect of our cooperation will make our friendship and trust stronger and greater." Signed by Sefer Halilovic. So can we link that up with the previous document and the order given on the 28th of January, which was P814? May we have your brief comments to this letter and Mr. Halilovic's views expressed there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: From this document, we can see that Mr. -- that the gentleman is informing the HVO Main Staff about the fact that cooperation is very good, and the spirit of communality, and that it is being continued, and in the previous document we see that he needs to remove the people that we were having good cooperation with. So it's not quite clear, what method the man is applying. However, immediately after this, four days later, there was an all-out attack against the HVO in Konjic, so things became clear to me on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, can you explain what actually happened in March, and when exactly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: On the 23rd of March, 1993, the BH Army attack against the HVO in Konjic started. In the morning, the Brigade Command was blocked and the Battalion Command was blocked, and so was the Military Police. And in the early morning hours, Zuka's units were in the area of Bradina, where our small barracks or training centre had been set up, and they arrested or took captive 35 of our fighters who were undergoing training over there. They did not put up any resistance. They were inside the facilities and premises. They confiscated their weapons and the MTS and brought these fighters to Bradina, to the school there, and held them in detention. According to what I knew, the information I had, this was certainly an attack that had been planned, and it was an attack of a broader scale. However, in the early-morning hours, the poor weather conditions - it was snowing - made it impossible for further activities that had been planned, for effecting them, and there was a lot of snowfall during the day so that the movement of troops and units were made completely impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, what happened in the town itself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: I've already said that. In the morning hours, the Brigade Command was blocked, as well as the Battalion Command and the Military Police, and in town members of the units, the Suad Alic Brigade, arrested people, confiscated HVOs -- confiscated weapons from HVO soldiers, and on that day about 150 of our soldiers were disarmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What happened next? Did the conflict cease that day in the area of responsibility where you were? What happened next on that day, during the day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: That same day and the following day, joint meetings were held in Konjic in order to deal with the situation and calm things down. Several meetings were held, and on the 25th of March, in Konjic, Bruno Stojic arrived, as did Milivoj Petkovic and Arif Pasalic, to size up the situation in Konjic and to do their best to calm the situation down. They held a joint meeting in town. I wasn't there at the meeting. But after the meeting, these gentlemen, together with a mixed group from the BH Army and the HVO, I mean, they started touring the positions where some trenches had been dug, and they, themselves, took part in filling in the trenches. I was in one of those areas. It was the area of Orlovica [phoen], at the foot of Batar [phoen]. And I'd just like to mention that this combat activity took place in the area of Operation Klis, which is the area of responsibility of the 1st Battalion, and there was much heavier fighting in Klis, up there in that area, and the brigade commander there was Zdravko Sagolj.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now take a look at the next document, which is 2D2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I said that all this was very complicated, but this is really an understatement. We have a document signed by Halilovic, dated March 17, 1993, sent to the Main Staff of the HVO in Mostar. In this document, Halilovic is recalling the friendship uniting the HVO and the ABiH, and now you're telling us that just a few days after this, there was an all-out attack, and then we discover that a few days later Mr. Stojic came on site with Pasalic and others to cool things down. It's almost impossible to understand anything. Either everyone is playing games, Halilovic is lying, saying, on the one hand, We're for peace, we're for friendship, and is not actually walking his talk; or there is another explanation which may involve the HVO and the ABiH. Behind the heads, there are other people who have their own agendas and who are doing what they can for their own agenda, and so they seem -- they just put fire on the keg of powder, and then the heads have to come over to try and cool things down. Now, you were there on the field. You were in the brigade, you played a role in the brigade. So could you tell us what your opinion is? Do you believe that these attacks had been ordered by the very top echelons or do you believe that these were just attacks that had been triggered at local level by a number of military leaders that were more or less under control, and when these attacks occurred, everybody had to chip in in order to try and cool things down? What do you think is the actual true version of facts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Within my remit and as far as I'm able to assess the situation at the time, I can just say, loud and clear, that at that time this man, Sefer Halilovic, gave false information in what he said. And let me just add that I have my suspicions that the conflict was staged at the very top, at the very peaks of the BH Army in Sarajevo, because if Sefer Halilovic was working for the Supreme Command of the BH Army, then this leads me to believe that that was the case. So those were my suspicions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Juric, following on from Judge Antonetti's question, whether it was planned and who planned it and so on, how the attack came about, let's look at 2D253, which is the next document. You have already seen the document. We looked at it during the proofing session. This document was -- is dated the 20th of March, and it's about a joint meeting with representatives of the BH Army commands, the Suad Alic, the Neretvica and Neretva Brigade, and the document was signed by all the representatives of the units mentioned. Now, did you know these people, or most of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Now, this is an assessment of the situation in the area of Hadzici, Jablanica and Konjic, and I'd now like to draw your attention to some of the points in this document. And this is already an exhibit, so let's look at page 2 of the English and Croatian, point 5, where it says in Jablanica, Donje Selo, and Bradina, that at all times the men must be on the alert. Now, Mr. Juric, we're talking -- this meeting was held on the 20th of March, 1993. At that point in time, was there a conflict at all between you and the BH Army in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No, there wasn't, not yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, point 9 says the BH Army forces should prepare to take control of Zlatar urgently, and in point 13 it says: "Through the assistant commander for operative affairs and the chiefs of staff, and the Public Security Service, to device a plan for the united action of all our forces in the area, should the need arise." Now, Mr. Juric, why was -- well, let me ask you, did you know about this meeting at all, if you had good relations with the Suad Alic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: We did have very good relations. I did not know about this meeting, and I claim with certainty that this meeting was not held in Konjic. I don't know where it was held, but definitely not in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, what did these conclusions mean "especially prepare army forces to take up Zlatar facility urgently"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: That was the plan, to take up and occupy that position, because that was our communications centre. By taking up that facility, we would no longer have any communication lines with the operations zone or with our units.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, in that attack on the 23rd of March, was that facility occupied?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No, because as I have said earlier, the bad weather most likely was the factor in not allowing them to reach that facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was there later another operation during which this facility, Zlatar, was taken up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was later, when there was an all-out offensive against the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. We will skip over some documents, and now please look at 4D -- that's the next document in your binder --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me intervene, please. We did not record the entire answer of this witness. The witness said that this attack began between the 13th and 14th of April, 1993, and these dates were not recorded in the transcript. So could the witness please repeat the dates that he mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you to my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, did you say that the new attack was between -- was commenced between the 13th and 14th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please look at just two more documents in relation to this attack from March. Would you please look at 4D438. Let me know when you have found the document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Who signed this report to the 4th Corps? It was signed by Midhat Cerovac, and he was the commander of Suad Alic Brigade at the time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And he says that he's hereby informing you about the situation in the area of responsibility of your brigade; 115 of the HVO captured; town blocked; the life and town paralysed. "We continue with arrests." Was that how it was, Mr. Juric, according to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, would you please skip over a couple of documents. You said that soon thereafter, a commission arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, the interpreter is asking you to slow down. You're going too fast.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I lingered on some topics due to additional questions, and this is why I need to hurry up now. I will slow down, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, would you please look at 2D463 [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, this is a report by Veso Vegar. You said that on the 25th of March, 1993, Mr. Bruno Stojic came to Konjic, as did Mr. Petkovic, and here we have the names of some other persons. And then in the last paragraph, it says that a joint commission, three-member commission, was established, a commission of the HVO and the BH Army, and its task was to tour the area engulfed by war activities and to establish the facts on the ground. And then it says the commission -- after the meeting, the officials of the HVO and the BH Army went to tour the ground, went on the field. Were you present when they were touring the situation in the field?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I've already stated so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I will correct the number in the transcript. The number of this document is 2D643. There was a permutation of numbers. Now, let us turn to April of 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before moving on to the months of April, I would like to discuss the months of March. We can see that an incident took place and that the authorities intervene. In document 2D253, we can see that the army representatives assess the causes of the conflict, and they mention a parallel authority which gave rise to a different tax system, different license plates, and traffic control by the HVO and so on and so form. So the reasons that led to the conflict are analysed, and then on the other hand, we see that the authorities intervened, and this is where I am at a loss. As far as you are concerned, in this municipality of Konjic, did you have the feeling that the HVO, with its taxation system and license plates, had created the conditions for the conflict to erupt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in this document that you are now referring to, what they describe is the political situation that I'm not familiar enough in order to be able to comment on it. If you're referring to the meeting, I haven't found it yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, when Mr. Petkovic came on the spot, did you actually see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the last time I saw him, when he came to cover up the trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you remember -- my question is a difficult question, because it's difficult to remember what was said 15 years ago. But as far as you remember, what did General Petkovic say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean General Petkovic, what they said? Well, they were in that commission, Stojic, Petkovic and Pasalic, and they never acted individually, any of them. Their joint appeal was the situation in Konjic had to calm down and conflict should not be allowed to erupt. There wasn't a lot of talk in those meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I have understood you well, because it's so complicated, then, when one piece is missing, it's very difficult to understand the whole story, it seems that Generals Petkovic and Stojic said that the trenches needed to be filled in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and they took up shovels and started filling it -- filling in trenches in some parts, in some positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Stojic and Mr. Petkovic picked up the shovels and filled in the trenches. When these trenches were dug in the first place, does this mean that this was done without the HVO Command being aware of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat? I haven't understood it quite --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me say it again. If General Petkovic and Mr. Stojic take a shovel and fill the trenches with soil, this means that they want to make sure that there are no trenches anymore. But when that happens, the trenches must have been dug before that, and could these trenches have been dug without them knowing about it? They didn't know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was at a local level in Konjic. This is why they came to tell us that the trenches were being filled in, and that they shouldn't exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may allow another intervention, once again not the entire answer was recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As soon as Mr. Petkovic's name is mentioned, you stand up. What is it you would like to say? Fortunately, I didn't mention Mr. Prlic. Otherwise, Mr. Karnavas would have stood up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may remind you, Your Honours, I intervened a bit earlier because of the wrong interpretation, and it had nothing to do with General Petkovic. Once again, not the entire answer was recorded. He first said not -- they didn't know that that was at a local level, not -- "they didn't know that" was missing, and I think it's important for you to understand completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In French, I heard, no, he didn't know about it. This is why I continued along those lines. Thank you very much for this clarification. At any rate, it's an important point, it's important that it's on the transcript. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my colleague. I was going to intervene, but she did it before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said, Mr. Juric, that conflicts erupted again in April. Let me ask you now, from that conflict on the 23rd of March, 1993, did the situation calm down until the following attack which took place between the 13th and the 14th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Somewhat. The situation in Konjic calmed down quickly, because during that conflict there were no victims in Konjic whatsoever. However, the situation in the area of responsibility of the 1st Battalion in Klis was quite complicated, because there were victims there, so that even after that agreement, there were occasional movements of units and there was occasional firing. There were victims only in the first conflict, and later on there were no further victims, but there were movements of units. So that was the area of responsibility in Klis of the 1st Battalion, where the commander of the battalion, Zdravko Sagolj, was located.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have I understood you well? You said in the area of responsibility of the 1st Battalion, there were victims initially?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And later on, there was only movement of units, but there were no conflicts, no victims? Have I understood you well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Juric, can you explain what happened between the 13th and the 14th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Between the 13th and 14th of April, 1993, is when an all-out attack of the BH Army against HVO began. In the town of Konjic, in the morning hours, they captured officers of the brigade who were there on their posts, and also members of the Battalion Command, and also the security forces. All in all, they captured 15 people that morning. And then in the course of the day, they started with operations to take up the Zlatar facility and to attack the edges of Konjic, where Croatian villages were located, Retica [phoen], Galjevo [phoen], Donje Selo, Pokojiste. On that day, soldiers of the HVO who were not manning positions facing the Army of Republika Srpska, organised the defence of their villages and hamlets, and I found myself among those soldiers because my house was in that sector as well. We put up resistance. We organised defence around our houses. The combat lasted for four days. The BH Army brought in new forces every day, and our defence was weakening. After four days of combat, we had 20 -- or, rather, 7 fatalities and 10 wounded slightly. During the 18th of April, we decided to cross over to the left bank of the Neretva towards the villages of Zaslivlje, Turije and Zabrdje. We had a large number of civilians, and our main duty was to protect and save those civilians and to transfer them across the Neretva, so this operation lasted some 14 hours, which is to say that on the 18th we withdrew from our positions, we abandoned the right bank of the river and crossed over to the left bank to these three villages, Zaslivlje, Turije and Zabrdje.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Chamber, why did you cross over to this particular area, or did you have any other choice? Were you deported, expelled from that area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Had we remained on the right bank, we would have all been arrested and taken to a camp, because throughout the duration of this operation, they were making announcements on the radio that HVO soldiers should disarm and place themselves under the command of the BH Army. We crossed into this other area because, in our view, it was possible to organise some sort of defence in that area. We believed that we were not far from Konjic and that eventually we would be able to return back to our homes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What happened with other soldiers of the HVO and Croat civilians in Konjic? Did you have any information about them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: In the course of the night, after we crossed, on the following day we started urgently organising and setting up defence in that territory. The area where we crossed to was just as steep as the part on the other bank. If one looks at the Neretva River, one could see the river flowing, and then there were mild slopes on both banks and we could have good visibility from that area, so that on the following day we could follow and we could watch what happened to soldiers and civilians who had remained on the other side of Neretva. In the course of the day, the civilians and soldiers were taken from there to the sector of the village of Gradina where they were taken to interrogation. Sometime in the afternoon, a group of people was lined up. In my view, there were more than 150 people in that group, and they were taken to the village of Homolje and then on to a camp in the sports hall in Konjic. Among those 150 - later on we learned there were also 10 Serb civilians among them - civilians were released to go home in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What happened? Did these civilians cross over later -- oh, let me ask you this first: How long did you remain in that area, Turije, Zabrdje and Zaslivlje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: A full 11 months.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: How many civilians crossed over, all in all, together with those who initially crossed over with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Initially, about 600 civilians crossed over, including 150 Serb civilians. And later on, in the course of 11 months, another 800 civilians came to us -- about 800 civilians came to us in this new territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Tell me, please, what happened with the 1st and 3rd Battalion of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: On that same day when attack was carried out against our units in Konjic, an attack against the 1st Battalion in Klis was commenced as well. We learned about that only in 1993, once we left that area, because we had no contact -- no communication with them. And it was only that we were -- we were only able to see that there was fierce fighting going on in that area. Later on, we found out that the commander of the brigade was located precisely in the area of responsibility of that battalion in Kostajnica, and later on we learned what went on. We learned that the majority of civilians and soldiers managed to leave the area, and then they were putting up -- those who remained and were putting up defence until July were later captured and taken to the sports hall in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Ms. Nozica. We have to have our 20-minute break now. Looking at how much time you have left. You have something like 15 minutes left, I believe, 15 to 20 minutes, so see how you can use your time at best. I'm a little bit concerned, because the other Defence counsel will certainly cross-examine the witness, and the Prosecution will have two hours, and we have tomorrow still, but we need to finish tomorrow. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I truly apologise. I can see already that I will need an additional 15 minutes to the time allotted to me, because I had to go back to certain topics, but that won't exceed 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, well, if that's the case, I won't put questions to the witness in the future anymore. That's for you to say, is it better for the Judge to put the question or is it better for you to put the question. I am a good timekeeper, and I know that the other Defence counsel will need time, and if you ask for an extra 15 minutes, then the Prosecution will ask for an extra 15 minutes left. Whatever the case may be, the Registrar just told me that you've got exactly 16 minutes left, so please think about it. We're going to have our 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in view of the remark you made before the break, I do apologise. I hold your questions in high regard. Perhaps it was just my poor assessment of time. So I would like to request just an additional 15 minutes extra time, and I will, of course, try and get through everything I intended as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm awfully sorry, Ms. Nozica, it appears that I have been the cause for you having been interrupted. That was not my intention at all, and if you have not finished, I would encourage you to finish. Excuse me. There must have been a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I just requested that I be given 15 minutes over my time because I did not assess how much time I would need -- I did not assess that properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, the Trial Chamber deliberated and says that you still have 16 minutes. You had two hours, and we will not give you any extra time. You have 16 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, can you tell the Trial Chamber, just briefly, what kind of terrain you were forced to go to? What was in front of you, what was behind you? What was the kind of terrain there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Turije, Zaslivlje, and Zabrdje are about 24 kilometres of a very hilly terrain, with streams and hillocks, and there are about 300 various facilities or houses which can be -- in which people can live, and there were about a thousand inhabitants. And then there was a main road, the main road running from Konjic to Mostar above that, and we controlled part of the road for about 1500 metres. And then to the right you have the Neretva River. On the right bank of the Neretva River, you had the BH Army, and the Neretva River and the main road divided us for about 200 metres, as the crow flies. Now, behind our positions to the north -- or, rather, to the east was the Army of Republika Srpska, with its positions, so that we were under total encirclement, on the one hand, by the Army of Republika Srpska, and the BH Army on the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, did you have any communication whatsoever with the Defence Department and the Main Staff? And I'd like to mention here that you said that you stayed in the area for 11 months. So could you explain to us whether you had a radio, radio communication, or communication by road, or any other type of communication with the Main Staff and the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber, briefly, what your living conditions were like? Or let me put it this way: Did you have enough food?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No. What food we had, we distributed in small amounts, because there were a large number of civilians and the important thing was to give women, children and the elderly the food that we had. And if anything remained, then we'd distribute it among the fighters. Because we had the local population, they had some of their stores, and there were two or three shops in the area, so that we used the food that was stored in those shops to feed the population and distributed it in as fair a manner as possible so that people could have food equally, both the citizens and our men.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you have electricity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you receive any assistance from any international organisations in the form of food, medicines, or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: While I was the commander in the area, until the 3rd of March, 1993, I don't remember ever having received any assistance in the form of food or medicines.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, were you the commander in the area until the 3rd of March? Or, rather, until when were you the commander, and how were you appointed commander of the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: As we moved to this area, we held a meeting, an urgent meeting, as I've already said, and the -- I was the deputy commander of the brigade at the time, and they proposed that I become the commander, and so I appointed my assistants and closest aides.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And for how long did you remain commander in the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Until the 3rd of March, 1993. Or, rather, the 3rd of July, 1993, is what I meant to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that you stayed on in the area for 11 months. How did you come to leave the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: After the signing of the Washington Agreement, UNPROFOR pulled us out via Jablanica, Slatina, and further on towards Herzegovina in their APCs.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Now, my last topic. Your unit, in mid-June, did it capture some translators -- some interpreters of the UNHCR?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: I was informed towards the evening -- my assistant for security informed me that a group of our fighters, without anybody else's knowledge, without any orders, had captured four persons, among whom there were three interpreters and one driver, I believe; and he had to resort to the military police to save these people. And then he took them to the house that he worked in, where he was accommodated, and interviewed them. After the interview, we decided that we should keep these people in the area for a few days so that somebody could come to the area, because we'd been there for 60 days without anybody coming to see how we were doing. So we thought we'd keep them there and that somebody might turn up.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at a few documents, the first of which is 2D793. And, Mr. Juric, perhaps -- well, the document will come up on your screen. Perhaps you can rely on that. Here, you have it. It is signed by Mr. Stojic, and it is a command to Mr. Keza on the 16th of June, and it says: "With the aim to resolving the situation concerning the alleged capturing of interpreters of UN and EU." And to Mr. Keza representatives in Konjic to use his authority to have the following prisoners released. Now, Mr. Keza, did he arrive in your area during those days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, let's look at the next document, which is P2794, and it is a report from the Tactical Group Canarias. P2794 is the document, P, not 2D but P. Have you found it perhaps, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a report by the Canarias Tactical Group, and please look at point number 3, and underneath that it says "Jablanica-Konjic," which is on your page 4, page 4 of your version. And it says here that the UNHCR has made a breakthrough to the Konjic pocket, with the aim of holding a meeting, and it says a group of HVO soldiers threatened them with weapons and shot up into the air, capturing the interpreters. And it seems that the HVO soldiers who had captured the interpreters did so without the knowledge of the commander of the pocket; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, on page 2 of this same document, we have the names of the interpreters, and it says that contact has been established to resolve the incident and that two letters had been sent, one from General Lasic and the other from General Stojic, with an order to the commander of the pocket to free the prisoners. Did you ever receive one of these letters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: The UNPROFOR brought the General Lasic letter.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And did you act upon it? Did you free the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't free them. We responded to the letter, sent an answer, and said that we requested someone from a higher HVO level to come to the area to size up the situation and to see the situation we were in. So we insisted upon that, that somebody should come to the area with UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. And that explains the next document, which is P2804, so you can just take a look at that. And from that document, we can see that SpaBat did not manage to break through with Mr. Stojic's letter, and that fully confirms what you've just said. It is number 1, the area of influence on page 3, and two more documents remain. P2808 is the first of them. This, once again, is a report from the commander of the Rapid Intervention Forces, and the date of it is the 17th of June, 1993, and it is on page 4 of your version, where it says that the BH Army, under the heading "Jablanica-Konjic," that the BH Army did not authorise Mr. Keza's passage through the area, and it says that telephone communication was established by means of the Inmarsat, and that they talked to you, that Mr. Stojic talked to you and the command of SpaBat; and that you said that you would give a response with respect to the freeing of the prisoners at 1700 hours. Now, can you explain to the Trial Chamber why you gave them this answer and why you didn't meet their demands after talking to Mr. Stojic and the commander of SpaBat with respect to the freeing of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Let me emphasise right away that Mr. Stojic would not be able to order me directly to implement this order, and the fact that I carried on and left another one and a half hours of the dead-line was because we wanted to analyse the situation a little bit more in order to reach a final decision about what would be done in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: According to this document, it says that you said that there was another call at 1700 hours, and you said that the answer would be sent on the 18th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So after that, did you nevertheless decide to release the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, after these two or three days of negotiations, simply we decided that there was no longer the possibility of achieving anything, and then thanks to Mr. Stojic, who promised that we would receive food, even though it did not arrive, we released those people because, in any case, they were a burden to us up there, because we didn't have enough food for our own people, never mind also to feed the persons that we had imprisoned in that area or were holding in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at the last document. This is P2826, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may just interject a question. Mr. Juric, did you at all think on the legal situation, on whether you were entitled to detain these people? Did that cross your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we did think about that also, but we were simply afraid for the security of those people if we were to release them from the area, that somebody else might detain them and ultimately neutralise them, and that later then we would be the ones to bear responsibility and to be accused of committing such a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And it didn't cross your mind that they could take their responsibility, themselves; you simply let them free, and they either go or stay and assess the danger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't think about that. And while they were with us in that area, they didn't really complain all that much that they were having a bad time while they were sitting there with us and talking, because they also saw the situation that we were in. And, simply, they too felt sorry for us, expecting that they would be able to help us as much as they could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you are part of a military structure. Some interpreters are captured, interpreters who belong to the UN. Your authorities orders you to release them, and you say that you wanted to meet up with the authorities to address some issues. Do you know that during, first, World War I, and I'm sure that this also occurred during World War II, that there were situations where those who did this were actually placed with their back to the wall and shot for insubordination? So if you thought that it was possible for you to have this kind of behaviour towards your authority, this means that your hierarchy was not able to control you, actually? This is what it seems to mean.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the area where we were, nobody could issue orders to us, and we were not able to submit a report to anyone. We were cut off from everyone. We could communicate through letters or memos or telegrams via UNPROFOR, so we were -- we decided to do this as a measure of desperation, because our situation there in that area at the time was desperate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I showed document P2794, P2794. It's a document under seal, so can we please do what is required in relation to that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said, sir, that Mr. Stojic would not be able to issue orders to you. In view of Judge Antonetti's question, I'm going to come back to that. But you said you did that because you were promised you would receive food. Can we now look at P2826, please. Have you found the document? This document is also under seal, so can we please not show the document outside the courtroom. Sir, have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We have some instructions or directives on procedure or work, and this is on page 2 in your document, where it says that Mr. Stojic used all of his persuasion -- powers of persuasion to try to work on the release of these persons. And then it says: "In the last two months the HVO commander in the pocket has been out of connection. He acted on his own, without any instructions or coordination from the HVO HQ." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It says: "Mr. Stojic promised to the commander, who was desperate for food and medicine, that he will assist him on this issue. Mr. Stojic committed himself to go with me to the area," with the person who wrote this document, "to the area with a convoy of supplies." You, yourself, said you did not receive that convoy of supplies. And also it says here that Mr. Stojic promised that he would provide this assistance. I'm going to ask you, again: If you did answer that, why did you finally decide to do what you did? There was a promise, wasn't there, that was made?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Well, we were thinking that if the promise was firm that it would also be fulfilled, but as it was, things stayed the way they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, can you please tell us, could you be reached without the assistance of international forces, who controlled the roads beneath the pocket where you happened to be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: It was the B and H Army from Jablanica to the place where we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In any other way, other than the army territory or through the territory controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska, was it possible to reach the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And, finally, can you explain to the Trial Chamber, first, did you receive an order from anyone -- did you receive an order from Mr. Stojic, and did Mr. Stojic -- was Mr. Stojic in a position to issue orders to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: I already said that my immediate superior was the commander of the brigade. If he was absent, then the next person in line would be the commander of the operations zone or the person of the Main Staff. So I respected Mr. Stojic for the duties that he was carrying out, but he was not in a position to issue orders to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have significantly cut short my questions and I have finished, in respect of your -- in adherence to your decision, and I have even finished two minutes before the time that was allotted to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's move to 3D.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for our internal order, I would like to state that Mr. Coric's Defence has no questions, just to avoid any kind of confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, you're standing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the purposes of the transcript, Mr. President, I would just like to say we have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Karnavas, 1D.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. We have no questions for the gentleman, although we do wish to thank him for coming here to give his evidence. Thank you very much, and good luck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. Good day to everyone in the courtroom. I would just like the usher to distribute the documents. I just have questions for the witness for about two or three minutes that have to do with the authenticity of the documents relating to his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Juric. I am representing General Praljak. We had the opportunity to meet briefly when you were in The Hague last time. I would like to ask you to look at this document first. Look at it carefully. Look at the person who signed the document. Look at the memo, whom it's addressed to for the beginning, and, of course, please look at the date. The number of the document is 3D03519. It seems, on the basis of this document, that it was written on the 14th of October, 1992. To avoid any kind of misunderstanding, at the time the HVO and the B and H Army or, rather, the TO and the army jointly were defending the area where you were from, the JNA aggression; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Kovacic. I read "14/11/92," and that would be November rather than October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right, Your Honour. In Croatian, I said the 14th of the 11th month, that is to say, the 14th of November, 1992, so it's a matter of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But I don't see the witness's answer recorded, so could you repeat and tell us if there were no conflicts between the HVO and the BH Army at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No, there were no conflicts between the BH Army and the HVO during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's see what's in the document. Let's look at the contents. Obviously, there was discussion between Maric and Mehmed Zilic, and you mentioned that link to the events in Konjic, and Arif Pasalic says that he is aware of the following elements: "We found out about the following elements." Anyway, it is a letter addressed to whom, please? Who is it addressed to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: The Municipal Staff of Mostar, the HVO Municipal Staff, Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, from this, do you consider that it is a fact that Arif Pasalic, writing to the HVO Municipal Staff of Mostar, confirms that there's complete cooperation between them at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And that agrees with what you knew of the situation at the time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Among other things, in the second line of the middle part of the text -- well, let's read it out. Pasalic says: "The BH Army units and the HVO Herceg Stjepan Brigade jointly elaborated a plan of activities in detail." And then he goes on to say: "They are waiting for Mr. Praljak's order." Now, can you tell me what activities or what plan of the -- what plan of the BH Army and HVO Herceg Stjepan Brigade is this? Did you know that there were joint plans with respect to certain operations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes. We compiled an order jointly for the liberation of the town of Konjic from the Army of Republika Srpska. It was an order for attack, and we compiled that together with the BH Army. We compiled the map and wrote out the order jointly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, within the plan, did the plan provide for the fact that General Praljak would launch the action, that it was up to him to decide when, when the operation would start?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure of that, so I can't say with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And do you know that General Praljak played a role in the plan to refute the Serbs from Konjic, the surrounding parts of Konjic, to push the Serbs back, in view of the fact that it says here they are waiting for Mr. Praljak's order? What does it mean, that line, that point, they're waiting for Mr. Praljak's order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that would mean that Mr. Praljak was to give the green light for the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Now, the individuals mentioned here, Stanko Maric and Mehmed Zilic, you mentioned them during your testimony. You know who they are?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know Mr. Stanko Maric and Mr. Mehmed Zilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That completes my examination. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, where does this document come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document, as far as I remember off the top of my head, is the result of my own investigation. It was brought from Bosnia-Herzegovina, but I don't have the information to hand in greater detail. Perhaps Mr. Praljak has some additional information to give you, if you will allow him to speak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have any additional information about the document, but I would like to be allowed to ask a question. I'd like to ask the witness a question, myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before this date when the plan of attack was determined, did you see me in Konjic at all, and did you happen to know that with a joint team from the BH Army and the HVO, I carried out reconnaissance in the area, the area that we were supposed to liberate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, and we met, and you came to the headquarters. I saw you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And there's another document that testifies -- well, I don't know why we didn't look at this other document. It should be put up on the ELMO. It testifies that the beginning of the operation --

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, do you remember that it was a joint operation, devised jointly, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to the Trial Chamber and everybody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. I'm going to give you the floor, but I am turning to the witness. Witness, if I have understood you well, around the months of November, or a few days before the 14th, you met General Praljak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Praljak came to Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who was he representing? Let me repeat. When he came, who was Mr. Praljak for you at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew that a man was coming from the Main Staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he came, was he a person with some authority or were there decisions taken by the local HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, but could you repeat your question? I am afraid my hearing isn't what it used to be, and that's why I speak fairly loudly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Mr. Praljak came, given your position at the time, did you feel that this was a man of authority who was coming, or was this somebody from the Main Staff of the HVO, and despite that, any decision would be taken by the local HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, I was the assistant chief for operations and training, and I was on duty in my brigade. I received the gentleman and reported about the numerical situation in Konjic. Now, I received the gentleman as somebody who had authority. He was the person who had authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Alaburic, we have 15 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we still have about 15 minutes left today, but I think that I will use the rest of the time that was allocated to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Juric, special greetings to you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We haven't had the opportunity to meet so far; is that correct, Mr. Juric?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. I know that Mr. Bruno Stojic's Defence is familiar with the documents on Konjic, prepared by the Petkovic Defence, so I hope that you are also familiar with those documents and that you will be able to comment on those documents. Mr. Juric, I'm only going to tell you this: I'm going to ask you exclusively about questions which you described on the 23rd of March, 1993, then the conflict in April 1993, and I'm going to show you some documents. I would like to draw your attention to parts of those documents, and I would like you just to say whether what is written in the documents corresponds to what you know, and if you don't know, then we're going to move to the next document without much discussion. The first series of documents has to do with the 23rd of March, 1993. On that day, if I understood you correctly, Mr. Juric, you said that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina attacked the HVO in the Konjic sector; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The first document that I prepared is 4D438. It was already shown to you by my learned friend Ms. Nozica, so we will skip it. Can you please look at the first document that follows. That's document 3D550.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In this document, the commander of the 7th Brigade, Suad Alic, Mr. Midhat Cerovac, informs the commander of the 4th Corps that: "Related to yesterday's arrests, we completely surrounded or blocked the town." The previous document that you already commented on contains the identical sentence. Mr. Juric, can you confirm that this document corresponds to what you really do know about the blockade of Konjic of that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at the next document, and that is 4D125, and that is document P1709. Mr. Juric, you spoke about how the joint commission of the HVO and the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army was formed and how members of that commission came to the Konjic area in those days. Can you please tell us if you saw this joint command of Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Pasalic before on behalf of the HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. The introduction of the order speaks about attempts to calm down tensions in certain areas. Can you please tell us whether these attempts to calm tensions in that area corresponds to what you know about the efforts of the military commanders of the two armies? Did they really try to calm down the tensions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you look at item 8, where it says: "The joint commission of the HVO and the BH Army that is being sent to you shall have all the powers in commanding." Did you know about the establishment of that commission which was supposed to come to your sector as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Now we're going to skip the next document that talks about that commission. That's document 2D638. We are going to skip that document, and we're going to skip the next document. Can you now please look at P1712, P1712. It's an interim report from the Rama Brigade, where it says dramatic news are arriving from Konjic about the situation in the town and that they are asking from Konjic that the Rama Brigade artillery opens fire at the villages that are noted here. Mr. Juric, can you please tell us, according to your knowledge, was the situation in Konjic on that day, the 23rd of March, really dramatic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes. That day, I already described the attack on our barracks in Bradina took place, and these villages also that are referred to here are in the area of responsibility of the 1st Battalion in Klisa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Juric, can you please tell us, if you know, that there was no artillery activity from the Rama Brigade, in spite of the requests from Konjic, on that day and the following days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: I don't think that there was, but I cannot be sure. I wasn't in Konjic. Where I was is quite a way from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Now we're going to move to March. This is document 4D872 [Realtime transcript read in error, "4D782"] that we're going to be looking at now. It's a report of the commander of the Klis 1st Brigade Mr. Zeljko Mlikota, for the 24th of March, 1993. Can you tell us, Mr. Juric, did you know Mr. Mlikota?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So he was really able to submit a report on behalf of this brigade, he had the authority to do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He did the Information and Propaganda Section in that area -- in that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In that letter, it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me for being precise, but here the document's number seems to be 4D00872 and not as it is written a few lines above, 782.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. I thank you, Your Honour Judge Trechsel. It is 4D872, and we're talking about the contents of the document.
