It's saying that the forces of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina from the morning have started intense firing at positions of the HVO, and then the military police of the HVO's blocked in Konjic, and the Command of the 2nd Battalion, and that "our flags are being burned in town," and HVO people or Croats were being arrested. Mr. Juric, can you please tell us, does this correspond to the actual situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes. We talked about that before, and I already described the events there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page and the beginning of the next page in the Croatian text, and that is the end of page 2 in the English text, it says: "We received information that the Suad Alic Brigade had been tasked to defeat us militarily at all positions around Konjic," or, rather, "on all the lines towards the Chetniks." Is this something that also corresponds to what you know about the situation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Members of this brigade, the Suad Alic Brigade, were disarming and arresting our fighters. I also mentioned how many were arrested that day; 150 of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, very well. Let's look at the next document, 4D554. Although you said that you didn't know about the commission that was formed according to the previous order, Mr. Juric, but did you know that there was a commission that came to the Konjic area, so that Petkovic and Pasalic came to that area as members of that commission? Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at what it says in this document. Mr. Arif Pasalic, on the 26th of March, 1993, it's a document in which he informs his superior, Sefer Halilovic, about the situation. The commission is tasked with monitoring and securing a cease-fire. The same is going to submit -- well, the sentence is not correct, an announcement by the public media. And now I'm going to read the last part: "Safet Cibo has arrived, and he will be connected in Jablanica and Konjic and will be continuing his further duties." Mr. Juric, do you ever hear the name Mr. Safet Cibo before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: That is Dr. Safet Cibo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us if this was the person who was the number one -- actually, who replaced the number-one person in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, Dr. Rusmir.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So we said that Mr. Safet Cibo replaced Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic. Mr. Juric, you said that Mr. Hadzihuseinovic was somebody who wanted to establish good relations with Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What would you say about Safet Cibo in that sense? Was he also that sort of person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: No. He had just come. He was sent from Sarajevo in order to cause the conflicts which actually did break out in March and April.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm going to skip the next document so that we can make the best use of our time. Let's look at document 4D434. It's a document after the one that we are skipping. There is a commission report here, and we can see the composition of the commission. It's sent to the Main Staff of the HVO on the 26th of March, 1993, and it says that the commission toured the crisis area in the broader region of Klis, removed the barricades, cooled the passions, halted the fire, and partially withdrew the army to their initial positions. And even though Klis is mentioned here, Mr. Juric, and you were not there, does that correspond to what you know about the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, because our commander, Zdravko Sagolj, told us that a commission had come to Klis and had toured these sections.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we look at 2D645. That's the next document. Again, the representatives of the joint commission of the Army of the BiH and the HVO, on the 28th of March, 1993, are informing their superiors about the situation, and it says -- well, they mention the villages that the commission toured during the day, and it says that in the crisis areas, local commissions were formed, which are working on filling in the trenches and restoration of trust. Mr. Juric, what you read here, does that correspond to the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now look at the next document, P1810, 1810. It's a joint report of the Main Staff of the HVO for the 4th of April, 1993. Let's look at page 3, the report pertaining to Konjic. In the English text, this is also on page 3, and it says here, amongst other things, that members of the B and H Army commission did not show up in Klis. They had a meeting at a motel in Konjic at 1600 hours, where the newly-appointed mayor was supposed to be presented to the commanders of brigades of the B and H Army. Mr. Juric, can you please tell us if this mayor who is being referred to here is perhaps Mr. Safet Cibo whom we mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it seems to me that it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says -- we're going to skip a paragraph, and then it says Croats are not allowed to pass the check-point at Oracac [phoen] under the pretext that moving out is being prevented in this way. A group of members of the B and H Army got into Prijeslop village at about 1800 hours. They were destroying things, plundering, and expelling women and children who were still in the village. So from this last piece of the text that we read, it seems that in April 1993, in spite of everything, there were certain provocations and incidents in the Konjic sector provoked or caused by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct, and I also pointed that out, that in Konjic itself and in the area around Konjic, there were no such incidents, although tensions were high. But I did say that in this area of responsibility in Klis, conflicts continued, and they continued throughout this whole period.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the next document. It's 2D774. It's a report from the 1st Brigade of -- the 1st Battalion of Klisa, and it's sent to the Main Staff and the command of the operations zone for the previous day. It says that there were occasional provocations. The village of Gornji Prijeslop and Aleksin Han are mentioned, and it says that HVO members and the barracks were fired at, and there was intense entrenchment of Muslim forces that was reported. I'm not going to read any more. My question, Mr. Juric, is: Are you aware of these events, and do they confirm your assertions that there were incidents which kept growing in number and significance in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We have time for one more document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. No, you have no more time, because it is now 7.00. A follow-up question for you, Witness. In this document, it says: "We cannot discard the idea that a member of KOS may be present." I assume this has to do with Jusa Hadzajlic, nicknamed Homeini. The fact that this is mentioned, well, does this mean that as far as the HVO in Konjic is concerned - you were a member of the HVO - you could not discard the idea that the Serbs, through their intelligence services or counter-intelligence, were manipulating some people to fuel the conflict? Is this what this means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, Your Honours. If you can repeat your question. I'm not quite sure I understand the whole question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every time I put a question --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you permit me, Your Honour, I would like to put the same question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Based on this document, Mr. Juric, it can be concluded that this gentleman who is mentioned here, Jusa Hadzajlic, could perhaps be a member of the KOS, and then that begs the question that members of the HVO, you and your colleagues, believed that some events, or some clashes with the Bosnia-Herzegovina Army were actually a consequence of KOS activity, that they were -- there were provocations organised in advance in order to provoke conflicts between the Muslims and the HVO, all under KOS organisation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JURIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you put the question to me again?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Perhaps we can do it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put the question tomorrow. Ms. Alaburic, you can put the question to the witness again. I have the feeling that things run more smoothly when you put the question. Witness, you will therefore be coming back tomorrow. We shall be sitting in the morning, and we will start at 9.00. According to the calculations of the Registrar, there will be 40 minutes left for cross-examination. I wish you all a pleasant evening, and we shall meet again tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of April, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: [The accused Prlic and Coric not present]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
